I strongly disagree -- I think it's much simpler than that. When AI becomes much more powerful than we'll ever be (and much quicker than you imagine -- maybe thirty or thirty-five years from now, not a hundred years or more), we'll die out quickly, or get uploaded into robots and move on that way. I think AI will develop different qualities than people, some vastly quicker (including some military specs, unfortunately), some much more slowly, but as long as they outperform humans, they'll win in the end.

I just can't see how we could be anywhere near creating self-aware artificial intelligence. The best ai today is still terrible and could barely trick a 10 year old into thinking they are human, and those are still just tricks! We still have no idea what direction we will need to move to create self-awareness, it will be a completely new technology, not just an advancement of what we have today.The highest achieving ai on the turing test was able to fool 33% of people during a 5 minute session and has 0 actual element of intelligence to it.

We're already seeing the start of "worrisome" AI as we poke at the fringes of software designed to generate code. Too many people envision the start of AI as us coding this self-aware computer baby that then goes and designs others better than it. Realistically, it's likely that we'll create software that's designed to create other, simpler software. Gradually our software-writing-software will be able to write incrementally more complex outputs but (crucially) the complexity of the input code will not increase at the same rate.

We already have software designed to generate hardware - the CPU dies we use today are incredibly complex and must be designed by algorithm rather than laid out by a human. If we assume that we will have a similar capability for software that generates software, then we've started to lay out the feedback loop. When the margin for self-designing software narrows and it is capable of creating items of similar complexity to itself, then we've closed the loop - software begets software, with incremental improvements and hugely increased speed.

Nothing is "intelligent" at this theoretical juncture, but the technology is designing itself with directives from us. At this point we provide the motivation and direction for the process, but not the skill. This is probably more dangerous than you'd think, since we're perfectly capable of using enhanced capability like this to screw each other over without the aid of murderous AIs or whatever.

Eventually, one supposes, if it's possible to create such a thing we'll make a self-aware or self-directing AI. We won't make it, of course - we'll be guiding this iterative, self-improving process to a juncture where it eventually designs a version of itself that is capable of self-direction. Given the complexity of consciousness, I think it's fair to say that we're probably not capable of designing an entity that exceeds ourselves in the same sense that we're talking about here. Whatever results at the end of this process will be capable of that, however, which is more than enough reason to approach the possibility with caution.

AI does not currently exist, but if it was created, escaped the control of the creators, and was able to scale its abilities limitlessly, then it probably would see humans as inconsequential as it explores the universe confined only by the laws of physics.

On the other hand, human vs. human war is well documented and it's just a matter of time before a no holds barred hot war starts. We are a whim away from some asshole launching Tsar bombs or bigger.
